payload.claim: When the `git status` call itself fails (non-zero exit, or git erroring, e.g. from the very lock contention `--no-optional-locks` was added to avoid), `dirty` is computed as `False` rather than treated as unknown. This silently reports the checkout as clean and returns the bare `sha` with no `-dirty` suffix, even though the actual working tree state could not be determined. Contrast this with the `HEAD` read two lines above (lines 37-39), where the analogous failure returns `None` (no answer) rather than a false positive-for-clean; the two failure paths are handled inconsistently, so a transient status failure on a busy host can make a dirty engine checkout get recorded and shown in the pull request as a clean, pinned commit.
